schemes.official_name: FIELD Global Capstone (CAP), formerly FIELD Global Immersion
schemes.description: Semester-long Required Curriculum course in the MBA first year. HBS matches each Global Partner company with a diverse team of six students who design something new for the company's local end-user consumers, then spend a one-week immersion at the partner's location (11-18 May 2026) meeting the partner and local consumers.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: HBS MBA first-year (Required Curriculum) students; Boston-based section for those who cannot travel
schemes.delivery_format: Team project with partner company; on-campus sessions plus immersion abroad
schemes.project_evidence: Teams design a new product, service or customer experience concept for the partner's local consumers [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: Each company is matched with a team of six students [1][2].
schemes.employer_evidence: Partner companies are selected by HBS, each names a Project Manager, signs a project agreement with HBS, hosts the team and receives the proposal [1][2]. Pages state learning, not consulting, is the main goal.
schemes.partner_role: Hosts team; names project manager; sets consumer-focused project area; receives proposal
schemes.deliverable: Proposal for new product/service/customer experience presented to the partner
schemes.unresolved: Credit/assessment weight; number of partners in current year (pages cite 13 and 16 cities); what the partner formally receives; HBS handbook and course pages could not be opened by WebFetch (404 / wrong page), so quotes are from search-index text.

sources.title: 2.16 Field Global Capstone (CAP)

schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Master's in Computational Science and Engineering / Data Science (inferred; page does not state who must take it)
schemes.duration: One semester (Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 sections listed)
schemes.project_evidence: Teams of 3-4 on a real-world project with messy real datasets; examples with defined models/systems built [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: 'in groups of 3-4 on a real-world project' [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Course listing refers to progress communicated to a 'partner organization'; search result for a SEAS page says semester-long projects with 'client' organizations; examples of industry partners [1][2]. Whether external partners are the norm for every team is not stated.

schemes.named_partners: Biogen, Fluxedo, Spotify (c. 2017); Unspace (2024-25, from search summary)

schemes.unresolved: Whether compulsory for the CSE/Data Science master's; credit; current partner list; iacs.seas.harvard.edu/capstone and designfair pages returned 403 so were not read; partner-coverage wording is from the course listing and search summaries.

profile_md: Harvard's verified employer-linked group provision sits in separate professional-school and programme routes rather than a central scheme. The strongest is the HBS FIELD Global Capstone: a required first-year MBA course in which teams of six work with a partner company abroad to design a new product or service for local consumers (immersion 11-18 May 2026). The SEAS/IACS Computational Science and Engineering Capstone (APCOMP 297R) puts groups of 3-4 on real-world projects for partner organizations, with a Fall 2026 section listed and named past partners such as Biogen, Spotify and Unspace; whether it is compulsory is unknown. The Harvard Law School Dispute Systems Design Clinic fits all three criteria (teams of 2-3, weekly client meetings, final report) but is undated, so current delivery is unclear. The Kennedy School Policy Analysis Exercise is a compulsory MPP capstone for public or nonprofit clients, but sources conflict on whether students work alone or in small groups. The legacy lead, the Mindich Program in Engaged Scholarship, offers about 60 community-engaged undergraduate courses a year, but its pages do not show group projects with partner organizations, so it is recorded as an evidence gap. Nothing was found in the sciences. No undergraduate College route with live external group projects was verified. Reach is programme-level throughout, with no institution-wide mechanism evidenced.
gaps: Reduced-depth review (about 14 searches plus page fetches). Several Harvard pages returned 403/404 to WebFetch (iacs.seas capstone, designfair, HBS handbook), so some evidence is search-index text. Not covered: Mindich course-level projects (GOV 1022 etc.), Harvard Innovation Labs, HGSE, HSPH, Harvard Medical School, GSD studios, Harvard Law SPOs/other clinics, Harvard Extension, further SEAS and FAS undergraduate courses; further departmental instances likely.
